hints: Focus on the gas test first, as relighting a glowing splint is a classic test for oxygen, so ask which Group 2 compound releases oxygen on heating.
Recall that a Group 2 nitrate decomposes to a white metal oxide solid plus nitrogen dioxide and oxygen gases.
Count the different gases carefully, as two compounds of the same type will give the same gases, while mixing types will give three different gases.
walkthrough:
**Identify the key gas from the test**

That glowing splint test is telling you everything. Relighting means oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, is one of the products.

Of the common Group 2 compounds, only nitrates release $\text{O}_2$ on heating.

**Recall the three decomposition patterns**

Let's put the rules side by side in your mind.

Nitrate decomposition:
$$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
White solid $\text{MO}$, plus exactly two gases: $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$.

Carbonate decomposition:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
White solid $\text{MO}$, plus one gas: $\text{CO}_2$, which does not relight a splint.

**Apply the only two gases condition**

The mixture must give a white solid and only two different gases in total.

If both components are nitrates, both give $\text{MO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. The solids are both white oxides and the gases are the same two gases, so the total stays at two. That fits perfectly.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{MgCl}_2$ does not thermally decompose in this way, and $\text{CaCO}_3$ gives only $\text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$. That is only one gas, and $\text{CO}_2$ extinguishes a glowing splint, it does not relight it.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the clever trap. $\text{MgCO}_3$ gives $\text{CO}_2$, while $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ gives $\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. Together that is three different gaseous products ($\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{O}_2$), not two, so it fails the question condition.
options.C: Correct. Both $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ and $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ decompose as $2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. Both solids ($\text{MgO}$, $\text{CaO}$) are white, and both reactions produce the same two gases, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. $\text{O}_2$ relights the glowing splint.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{CaO}$ are already oxides and are thermally stable. They do not decompose further on heating, so no white solid is newly formed and no gases, including $\text{O}_2$, are produced.
